name: mdk
tagline: Native desktop apps in machin (MFL): GPUI-style GPU UI in one draw call per frame, hot reload that keeps state.
requires: FreeType + HarfBuzz dev packages (pkg-config freetype2 harfbuzz)

commands.does: scaffold an app directory with app.src (a counter)
build the app as a .so, open the window, rebuild on every save; the window and state survive; build errors draw over the last good frame
one release binary with the app linked in (no reload, sleeps when idle)

commands.cmd: ./mdk shot <appdir> out.ppm [--size W H] [--frames N] [--click X Y]...
commands.does: render N frames (clicks are real SDL events) and save a screenshot; convert out.ppm out.png to view
typecheck the app with the framework (machin encode), no window

app_contract: An app is a directory of .src files. mdk prepends framework/*.src and compiles them together with machin (encode concatenates files: that is the module system).
Define exactly one `func view()`. It runs every frame that needs drawing (input, resize, reload, or animate()).
Do not define main(). The framework exports mdk_frame, which wraps view() in arena { } so a frame's temporaries are freed when it returns.
Keep state in the host store: state_int/set_int, state_f/set_f, state_str/set_str. It survives every hot reload; MFL globals do not (they reset on reload).

Never assign per-frame values to MFL globals: inside the frame arena, a global assignment promotes the value out of it and leaks every frame. Assigning a global once (a cache filled on first frame) is fine.

Build the UI top-down every frame: open containers with col()/row(), add content, close with end(). Modifiers (gap, bg, pad, ...) apply to the LAST created element, or to the container just closed by end().
Widgets return their event for this frame: if button("Save") { ... }.

fns.name: col
fns.summary: open a vertical container (children top to bottom); returns its element index

fns.name: row
fns.summary: open a horizontal container (children left to right)

fns.name: end
fns.summary: close the innermost open container; following modifiers target it

fns.name: spacer
fns.summary: an empty element with grow 1: pushes siblings apart

fns.name: vlist
fns.sig: vlist(n int, row_h float, scroll float) -> (first int, count int)
fns.summary: open a virtualized list of n fixed-height rows scrolled to `scroll` px; build exactly rows first..first+count-1 (each height(row_h)), then end()

fns.name: text
fns.summary: one line of text at size px (shaped with HarfBuzz, cached)

fns.name: para
fns.summary: a paragraph: wraps at spaces to the width its container gives it

fns.name: label
fns.summary: text at the current element's font size

fns.name: button
fns.summary: accent button; true on the frame it is clicked (press and release inside)

fns.name: button_styled
fns.sig: button_styled(s string, base int, hover int, pressed int) -> bool
fns.summary: button with your own three colors

fns.name: fill
fns.summary: take all space on both axes (grow on the main axis, stretch on the cross axis)

fns.name: grow
fns.summary: share of the free main-axis space

fns.name: scroll_y
fns.summary: offset a vertical container's content by px

fns.name: radius
fns.summary: corner radius (SDF, crisp at any scale)

fns.name: state_int
fns.summary: read a host-owned int (default on first read)

fns.name: hovered
fns.summary: pointer is over element i (last frame's layout)

fns.name: pressed
fns.summary: button held after a press that started on i

fns.name: clicked
fns.summary: released this frame on i after pressing on i

fns.name: animate
fns.summary: ask for another frame right away (otherwise the app sleeps until input)

gotchas: machin typechecks reachably: an error in a function view() never calls does not fail the build (and draws no overlay).
MFL loops are `while cond { }`; there is no C-style for. Floats need a dot (16.0); int->float is float(i).
Struct types are `type T struct { ... }` with one field per line.
Colors are ints 0xRRGGBBAA; the alpha byte matters (0x...00 is invisible).
Modifiers apply to the last element: call them right after the element (or right after end() for a container).
Text is clipped by nothing yet: keep content inside the window, or use vlist for long lists.
To verify without a human: ./mdk shot <app> out.ppm --click X Y, then convert out.ppm out.png and look at it.
